packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response
text:
PACKET-05 - unverified blind image reading

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or
reading of this text. I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files in this packet
(plus a directory listing of the packet folder and a pixel-size check). I did
not use the web, any catalogue, or packet.json. I have not named the work or
its use; I have transcribed the sung text as seen and not completed phrases.

Conventions: (abc) = proposed expansion; word? = uncertain reading;
[illegible] = could not read; [?] = a letter group seen but not resolved;
[X]rest = enlarged initial X (red or red-touched) followed by the rest of the
word. Hyphens inside words (e.g. "fue-rit") mark syllables spaced out under
the notes, as on the leaf. Line numbers count text lines (not staff lines) from
the top of each tile; overlapping lines are marked "= image-NNN Lx".
"aevia" is written as such throughout (a recurring abbreviated word, usually
spelled "ae via" with the letters spaced under notes); I leave it unexpanded.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================
One leaf, two faces (overviews image-001 and image-006), portrait, single
block of writing (no columns). Every text line sits under a red-ruled staff
(4 red lines) carrying square/diamond and stroked neumes in brown-black ink;
custos-like marks at line ends. Gothic book hand, text in brown ink.
Sections begin with enlarged initials (some red, some brown with red
touches). Short red insertions in the text line at section breaks (e.g.
"Euou"/"Euouae"-type letter group, sometimes struck through in red; a red
"Ap(osto)l(orum)?" on face 1). Red vertical strokes divide pieces on the
staves. Red marginal sigla on face 2 right margin: "A" (x3), "R" (x3,
resembling a response sign), "[?]ew"?, "ad ix"?, "ad [?] / [?]s".
Face 1 (image-001): very large red initial I in the left margin running down
about 9 text lines (lines 11-19 of the page), with a red "C" beside its top;
faint brown "C" and "+" marks further left; modern ink/pencil at left margin
"1570" and "(Westbrunnen?)" (blue, modern), pencil "Stams, STA, Fog. 135r?"
(faint, upper left, vertical). At the foot, below the last notated line, two
unnotated ruled lines in a different, more cursive brown hand (later
addition). A horizontal fold crosses the middle (around text line 10).
Face 2 (image-006): pencil "Stams, STA, Fog. 135v?" (vertical, upper right);
".13." in the right margin beside text line 4; red marginal sigla as above;
small boxed "nn" above a word (image-009 L3), perhaps a correction.
Tentative interpretation: a notated service book with a series of short
chants (each opened by an initial), not prose with commentary.

======================================================================
SPANS SELECTED
======================================================================
All text lines on both faces (face 1: 16 notated text lines + 2 added lines;
face 2: 14 notated text lines). Weak areas: the fold zone on face 1
(image-003 L5, image-004 L2), the rubbed lines image-004 L6-L7 and image-005
L3-L5, and the added lines at the foot of face 1 (pale ink). The neumes are
not transcribed.

======================================================================
LIMITATIONS
======================================================================
- Musical notation not transcribed or checked; I read the text only.
- Fold and rubbing on face 1 weaken image-003 L5, image-004 L6-L7 and
  image-005 L3-L5; the added foot lines on face 1 are pale and partly guessed.
- Red insertions between pieces (the "Euou"-type groups, "Ap(osto)l(orum)?",
  "L(au)d(e)s?") and the red marginal sigla are read only tentatively.
- Initials identified from the following letters; where the initial's form is
  ambiguous it carries "?".
- Face order assumed from the pencil "r"/"v" notes as I read them; the
  bottom of face 1 ("... A[nnunciaverunt]? ...") does not obviously continue
  at the top of face 2 ("eos in no(m)i(n)e tuo ..."), and the top of face 1
  ("venia(m) ad vos ...") begins mid-phrase, so the face order may be the
  reverse (face 2 bottom "ne derelinquas orphanos sed" could lead into face 1
  top "venia(m) ad vos"). I note this without deciding.
- I did nothing beyond the brief's rules (beyond a directory listing of the
  packet folders and an image-size check).
